waivers.Utopia\\NATS\\Transport\\SwooleTransport: PHP runtime plumbing: the transport on Swoole's coroutine client, for PHP processes that disable Swoole's stream hooks. Every Rust transport is async on tokio, so TcpTransport and TlsTransport (whose behaviour transport.round_trip and every connection case cover) are what it is in Rust.
waivers.Utopia\\NATS\\Internal\\CallbackExceptio: PHP runtime plumbing: an @internal wrapper marking exceptions raised by callbacks while a request batch collects, so the batch rethrows them instead of reporting them as request outcomes. Rust carries the same distinction in Error::Callback; the behaviour is covered by the RequestsTest cases.
waivers.Utopia\\NATS\\Subscription::setConnectio: Accessor subsumed by Rust types: PHP links a Subscription back to its Connection after constructing it; a Rust subscription belongs to the connection that created it (Connection::subscribe), and the methods that need the connection are Connection methods.

deviations.php: Header names, values, the status line and the "Invalid header version" message keep whatever bytes the block holds, UTF-8 or not.
deviations.reason: utopia_nats::Headers holds String names and values (NATS headers are ASCII, MIME-style text). Bytes that are not UTF-8 become U+FFFD, in the parsed headers and in the error message. The fuzz profiles generate UTF-8 header blocks.

deviations.php: The subject, sid and reply subject of a MSG/HMSG line, an -ERR text and the line quoted in an "Unknown protocol operation" message keep their bytes, UTF-8 or not.
deviations.reason: utopia_nats::protocol::RawMessage and Message hold String subjects (NATS subjects are UTF-8 text); bytes that are not UTF-8 become U+FFFD. Payloads stay bytes exactly. The fuzz profiles generate UTF-8 control lines with arbitrary payloads.

deviations.php: Requests that are not Request objects, or not a list, and an infinite or NaN timeout raise InvalidArgumentException; a callback that reads the connection (request, processMessage, requestMany, wait, flush, tick, drain, requestBatch) while the batch collects raises LogicException.
deviations.reason: request_batch takes &[Request] and an Option<Duration>, so the first are unrepresentable (a zero timeout still raises InvalidArgument, as in PHP), and the reply callback borrows nothing of the connection: the borrow checker rejects a nested read at compile time rather than at run time.

deviations.php: After a failed STARTTLS handshake the stream stays open in plain text, holding whatever the TLS attempt left unread.
deviations.reason: tokio-rustls consumes the TCP stream for the handshake and drops it when the handshake fails, so the Rust transport is closed afterwards (writes and reads fail with "Not connected"). Both raise "Failed to upgrade connection to TLS"; the case stops there.

deviations.php: Timeouts, intervals and waits are float seconds; negative, infinite and NaN values are accepted (and make the PHP stream calls misbehave).
deviations.reason: utopia_nats::ConnectionOptions uses std::time::Duration, which is finite and non-negative. The cases use the float values Duration represents.

bound.server_request: A round trip to the NATS server (out to the subscriber and back), the same on both runtimes, dominates the call
